Weekends are prime real estate, and with summer sadly on it’s way out, we’re not about to waste our time on mediocre plans. Your Saturdays and Sundays deserve main character energy, not “guess we’ll just wander around” vibes.

Lucky for you, the city is stacked right now. We’re talking pop-ups, outdoor festivals, rooftop hangs, new bites, and exhibits that are actually worth leaving your apartment for. Ready to make some plans?
And if your weekend mood says “out of office,” we’ve got plenty of summer getaway ideas waiting too:
Only 1.5 hours from NYC, this ‘tropical paradise’ waterpark is now open — featuring a 1-million-gallon wave pool and one of the country’s largest lazy rivers
This quiet 46,283-acre preserve in the eastern Adirondacks is the ultimate summer escape — with crystal-clear waters and miles of shaded forest trails
This crystal clear lake near NYC called the ‘Caribbean of NY’ opens for swimming this weekend—& it’s home to a hyper-rare ‘coral reef’
‘America’s best beach’ is located in New York, just a short, scenic train ride from Manhattan — famous for its white sand, crystal-clear water, and Gilded Age mansions
— With contributions from Sydney Hargrove and Corey Fuller
Dive 12,000 feet underwater in NYC’s new Titanic VR experience
Photo courtesy of Titanic: Echoes From The Past
Eclipso NYC

Step aboard the Titanic, explore its historic interiors, and descend 12,500 feet beneath the Atlantic in this immersive VR experience that brings the ship’s story to life through cutting-edge technology and guided storytelling!
Celebrate Italian culture at the Ferragosto Festival on Arthur Avenue
Belmont Business Improvement District
Arthur Avenue (between East 187th Street and Crescent Avenue)
If you’re looking for an easy, food-filled Sunday plan, the annual Ferragosto Festival returns to Arthur Avenue with authentic Italian food, live music, and old‑world street fair vibes this weekend.
The massive street fair takes place Sunday, September 13 from 12 pm to 6 pm on Arthur Avenue between East 187th Street and Crescent Avenue. Learn more.
Feast on $1 dumplings at the 14th annual Jackson Heights Momo Crawl
Source / SFTHQ, @usherpa
Diversity Plaza (Jackson Heights)
Taste $1 momos from 30+ Himalayan vendors at Jackson Heights’ biggest momo festival.

One of the tastiest picks for your NYC weekend plans, the Momo Crawl returns Sunday, September 13, 2026 at Diversity Plaza in Jackson Heights, featuring 30+ Tibetan, Nepalese, and South Asian vendors serving $1 momos.
Participation requires a Momo Crawl Passport ($15–$60), with proceeds supporting Students for a Free Tibet.
Build big at the Creative Time Sandcastle Competition in the Rockaways
Photo by Derek Schultz. Courtesy of Creative Time.
Beach 108th Street shoreline (Rockaway Beach)

For a classic end-of-summer beach day with a creative twist, Creative Time is reviving its Sandcastle Competition on Sunday, September 13, 2026, bringing artists and locals to the Beach 108th Street shoreline in the Rockaways for a public sand-sculpting event.
Learn more.
Get an exclusive shade-matching experience with Fenty Beauty
Source / Fenty Beauty
262 Mott Street

On Saturday, September 12, from 10 am to 11:30 am, receive an exclusive shade-matching experience with Fenty Beauty, where you’ll have the opportunity to discover your perfect match and learn more about the newest addition to the Pro Filt’r franchise.
Book a luxury glamping stay just 8 minutes from Manhattan—with waterfront yoga, nightly s’mores, and skyline views
Source / Collective Retreats
Collective Retreats Governors Island
Who says you have to leave NYC for a proper summer escape?

Just an eight-minute ferry ride from Lower Manhattan, Collective Retreats Governors Island offers a glamping getaway with luxury tents, cozy cabins, glass-walled suites, waterfront dining, sunrise yoga, live music, and nightly s’mores—all set against postcard-worthy views of the Statue of Liberty and the Manhattan skyline.
It feels worlds away from the city, yet it’s one of the easiest staycations you’ll ever take. Learn more.
Grab a complimentary ice cream cone at the Flex Ice Cream pop-up truck
Source / Flex Ice Cream
Washington Square Park, between University Place + Fifth Ave
Flex–the #1 selling menstrual cup and disc brand in the U.S.–is inviting New Yorkers to stop by their pop-up ice cream truck on Saturday, September 12th from 11 am to 4 pm.
Expect complimentary frozen treats, Flex goodies, a photo moment, and more.
Dance through DUMBO at NYC’s new immersive silent disco
Source / The Circuit
Superfine – 126 Front St, Brooklyn, NY

Trade the traditional dance floor for the cobblestone streets of DUMBO at The Circuit, a one-of-a-kind silent disco that blends live theater, contemporary dance, and an EDM soundtrack delivered through wireless headphones!

As performers lead guests through Brooklyn’s waterfront neighborhood, the city transforms into a living stage—culminating in an immersive, high-energy experience that’s equal parts nightlife, art, and party.
Get tickets here.
Score goodies at Haus Labs and Sephora’s first-ever pop-up during New York Fashion Week
Source / Haus Labs x Sephora
76 Greene Street
Haus Labs and Sephora are taking over SoHo for the brand’s first-ever New York City pop-up during New York Fashion Week, a special experience celebrating all things complexion.

From personalized shade matching and expert consultations to an immersive 51 Shades Wall and Haus Labs photo booth, beauty lovers will have the opportunity to discover their perfect complexion match and experience the brand firsthand.

The pop-up will spotlight Haus Labs’ expansive 51-shade complexion assortment, showcasing the brand’s commitment to innovative, high-performance complexion products created with a wide range of skin tones in mind.
Friday, September 11 | 12 pm – 6 pm
Saturday, September 12 | 12 pm – 6 pm

424 Fifth Avenue, Midtown
New Yorkers will travel surprisingly far for good food—and Midtown officially has a new reason to draw a crowd.

Shaver Hall opened on Friday, June 26 inside the landmark former Lord & Taylor flagship on Fifth Avenue, bringing 35,000 square feet of food, drinks, entertainment, and one very oversized cheese conveyor belt to the heart of Manhattan. From Brooklyn-style pizza and hand rolls to steakhouse dining and self-pour cocktails, the massive new food hall is packed with reasons to stop by.

Whether you’re coming for the world’s largest Pick & Cheese conveyor belt, one of its 14 food concepts, live music, or late-night drinks, here’s everything you need to know before the doors officially open this weekend.
Grab samples, merch, and more at the OLAPLEX NYC Pop-Up
Source / OLAPLEX
Flatiron Plaza – 23rd & Broadway
OLAPLEX just launched its first-ever hairspray, Shape Set, and is hosting a larger-than-life celebration in NYC this weekend.
The activation will include a photo-op and the opportunity to pick up samples of Shape Set and other OLAPLEX merch! The first 50 attendees will receive full-size samples of Shape Set.
Saturday, September 12 | 11 am – 5 pm
Sunday, September 13 | 11 am – 5 pm
Daydream at Balloon Museum
Photo Courtesy of Balloon Museum

The Seaport is now home to the Balloon Museum, the U.S. flagship location right here in NYC. The first exhibit, Daydream, spans across massive rooms filled with inflatable sculptures, light installations, and turns kids from passive observers into active participants.

Little ones (and adults alike) can bounce, wander, and physically interact with large-scale works by world-renowned contemporary artists. This is a rare cultural experience that feels equal parts high-art gallery and boundless sensory playground.
Eat your way through NYC’s top 100 restaurants for 2026, according to The New York Times
Source / Marcus Lloyd
If your weekend plans revolve around a great meal, New York City is a culinary paradise with its extensive range of restaurants–over 23,000 to choose from!
The New York Times’ 2026 list spotlights NYC’s top 100 dining destinations right now, spanning all five boroughs, countless cuisines, and every type of dining experience imaginable. Find it here.
Catch Broadway stars putting a theatrical spin on your favorite hits
Source / Katy Beth Barber – Kbarberphotography
Enter location
Whether you’re part of the BeyHive or still blasting Fleetwood Mac on repeat, Broadway Sings is bringing beloved pop and rock anthems to life with powerhouse vocals and a live orchestra.

Taking over The Cutting Room on select dates this month, the concert series transforms hits from Beyoncé, ABBA, Fleetwood Mac, KPop artists and more into unforgettable Broadway-style performances that music and theater fans alike won’t want to miss.
Upcoming shows:
Broadway Sings ABBA (September 17)
Fleetwood Mac: Stripped (September 23)
KPop: The Hunt Is On – A Live Concert Tribute (September 27)
…Or have a meal at one of the restaurants we’ve recently been loving
Source / Cecchi’s

Between the impossible-to-book tasting menus, beloved neighborhood staples, and hole-in-the-wall spots worth trekking across boroughs for, deciding where to eat next in NYC can practically feel like a full-time job. Thankfully, we’re here to help.
Here are some restaurants we’ve been loving lately:
Chama Mama (Multiple Locations) – a restaurant serving classic Georgian cuisine with a modern spin–definitely try the Adjaruli Khachapuri, any of the Khinkali, and the Pan Seared Trout!

Georgie’s Chelsea (Chelsea, 161 8th Ave) – an all-day neighborhood café with a downstairs hidden speakeasy-style cocktail lounge serving an elevated contemporary food menu, craft cocktails, and a relaxed but elevated ambiance
Cecchi’s (West Village, 105 W 13th St) – for happy hour leans into classic New York vibes, stunning murals by Jean-Pierre Villafañe, and a beautifully lit, sexy space
Seirēn (Chelsea, 94 7th Ave) – for a transportive, coastal feel to with a setup that leans into the spirit of a laid-back European aperitivo hour
Sing your heart out at Baby Grand
Source / Baby Grand
If you’re looking for a place to belt your lungs out, there’s no better than Baby Grand.
With two locations in New York City–the Lower East Side (187 Orchard St.) and Flatiron (29 W. 17th St.)–the open room atmosphere makes for the perfect place to show off your skills. Learn more.
Step into ARTE Museum’s immersive art at Chelsea Piers
Source / Arte Museum New York
61 Chelsea Piers
Experience classic masterpieces reborn through immersive light, sound, and motion.

If you’re looking for a mind-blowing indoor pick, ARTE Museum New York at Chelsea Piers brings Monet, Van Gogh, and Musée d’Orsay works to life using light, motion, and sound. The result:an immersive fusion of fine art and technology that transports visitors into art history.
Grab tickets here.
Enjoy free Friday nights at the Whitney Museum with art, drinks, music, and skyline views in the heart of the Meatpacking District
Source / The Whitney
99 Gansevoort Street
The Whitney Museum of American Art opens its doors for free every Friday evening from 5–10 pm, offering one of NYC’s easiest ways to spend a night surrounded by world-class contemporary art.

Alongside the galleries, visitors can enjoy special programming, music, drinks, and sweeping city views from the museum’s outdoor terraces—making it as much a social night out as a cultural one. Admission is free, but timed tickets are required and capacity is limited, so advance booking is highly recommended.
It’s the perfect low-key Friday plan in NYC: culture, skyline, and a little museum magic without the price tag. Learn more.
Head to date nights at The Met
Shutterstock / Alexander Prokopenko
1000 Fifth Avenue, New York

​​What could be better than an evening of outstanding art and time spent with your love bug? Friday and Saturday night dates at the Met not only include picturesque scenes but drinks, music, and more.
Make note: the fun gets underway from 5–9pm.
Join the Secret NYC book club for great reading recs
Add caption
Enter location
Need a new read? The Secret NYC book club via Fable has you covered. Check out what’s happening with the club and join our discussion!
Explore this NYC exhibit that recreates what the city looked like 400 years ago
Source / Before New York: The Natural Geography of the City (2026) & Getty Images (Eloi_Omella)
Enter location
If you were to rewind about 400 years, you’d barely recognize NYC–and the New York Botanical Garden’s new exhibit, Before New York, is bringing that long lost landscape back to life.
Based on more than two decades of research, the exhibit blends a mix of large-scale visuals with digital renderings to reimagine the city’s original landscape–one shaped entirely by nature.
It’s on view now through November 15, 2026 at NYBG’s Ross Gallery, but it will appear across all five boroughs throughout the year. Learn more.
See a new movie in theaters
Shutterstock / Karramba Production
Enter location

Add extra butter to your popcorn and grab a drink: the 2026 movie release lineup is one for the books: book-to-screen adaptations, blockbuster sequels, pop culture favorites and more await, including The Oydssey, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and Moana.
Laugh out loud at BATSU!
Source / BATSU!
67 1st Ave, New York, NY 10003

Looking for something wildly different to do this weekend? Check out BATSU!, a fast-paced, laugh-out-loud live comedy game show where comedians compete in ridiculous challenges, improv games, and over-the-top punishments.
It’s unpredictable, high energy, and feels like a party you’re watching (and sometimes yelling at) in real time. Perfect if you want something fun, chaotic, and totally memorable.
P.S. you can buy one ticket get one free by joining our Secret Club!
Headline your own game show in Times Square
Source / Great Big Game Show
1619 Broadway

Grab your friends, smash real buzzers, spin giant wheels, and battle through fast-paced mini games on a hidden soundstage–confetti and bragging rights included. If you’ve ever dreamed of being on a game show, this just-opened experience lets you live it IRL, and it’s perfect for a weekend win.
Catch a Broadway show
Add caption
Enter location
There’s never a shortage of shows on the Great White Way.

Whether you’re thinking of channeling your roots with Harry Potter And The Cursed Child, want to sing your heart out at Wicked, or prefer something a little more serious like The Outsiders, the selection is unparalleled.
Light up your weekend with a Candlelight Concert
Source / Candlelight Concerts
Trade the usual weekend plans for an evening surrounded by hundreds of flickering candles and live music at a Candlelight Concert in NYC.
Upcoming Candlelight concerts in NYC:
Sept. 11: Tribute to Michael Jackson
Sept. 12: Tribute to A.R. Rahman
Sept 13: Candlelight Babies: Classical Sounds to Stimulate Little Minds
Get tickets to The Met’s Under 40 program
Shutterstock / Stefano Politi Markovina
30 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York
For a sophisticated date night à la Ronnie Cammareri and Loretta Castorini, turn to the Met’s Fridays Under 40, one of the most unique experiences you can have on the Upper West Side.

The longstanding tradition makes opera more accessible to a younger crowd and provides a unique way to spend an evening. Every Friday, those who have yet to reach the big 4-0–yes, you’ll have to prove your age–can score tickets to classics like Le Nozze di Figaro, Antony and Cleopatra, and the mother of all performances, La Bohème, at a discounted rate.
Step inside the Mind of a Serial Killer exhibit
Source / Mind of a Serial Killer: The Experience
526 6th Avenue
Enter a gripping immersive exhibition that places you inside an FBI‑style case file.

If you’re in the mood for something seriously chilling this weekend, Mind of a Serial Killer: The Experience is an exhibition in NYC featuring reconstructed crime scenes, archival artifacts, and a VR investigation that immerses visitors in forensic casework.
Get tickets here.

Explore this NYC exhibit that recreates what the city looked like 400 years ago

Source / Before New York: The Natural Geography of the City (2026) & Getty Images (Eloi_Omella)

Enter location

If you were to rewind about 400 years, you’d barely recognize NYC–and the New York Botanical Garden’s new exhibit, Before New York, is bringing that long lost landscape back to life.


Based on more than two decades of research, the exhibit blends a mix of large-scale visuals with digital renderings to reimagine the city’s original landscape–one shaped entirely by nature.


It’s on view now through November 15, 2026 at NYBG’s Ross Gallery, but it will appear across all five boroughs throughout the year. Learn more.

Get tickets to The Met’s Under 40 program

Shutterstock / Stefano Politi Markovina

30 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York

For a sophisticated date night à la Ronnie Cammareri and Loretta Castorini, turn to the Met’s Fridays Under 40, one of the most unique experiences you can have on the Upper West Side.


The longstanding tradition makes opera more accessible to a younger crowd and provides a unique way to spend an evening. Every Friday, those who have yet to reach the big 4-0–yes, you’ll have to prove your age–can score tickets to classics like Le Nozze di Figaro, Antony and Cleopatra, and the mother of all performances, La Bohème, at a discounted rate.
